scores.label: A
scores.note: Option 2 'forces' overstates. Macbeth 'finally agrees', so he is not forced, and the meaning changes. Option 3 'demands him to kill' is ungrammatical in place. Option 4 'inspires' has the wrong positive sense, which changes the meaning. Options 7-10 are duplicate fails.

scores.label: B
scores.note: Option 2 'insists him to kill' is ungrammatical. Option 7 'compels' overstates and contradicts 'he finally agrees'. Option 8 'dissuades' means the opposite. Option 9 'coaxes him' doubles 'him' in the sentence. Option 10 'presses upon him to kill' is ungrammatical.

scores.label: C
scores.note: Option 5 'compels' overstates and contradicts 'he finally agrees'. Options 6-9 are duplicate fails and option 10 is an echo fail.

scores.label: D
scores.note: Option 3 'instigates him to kill' is an odd, archaic construction for this essay. Option 5 'compels' overstates and contradicts 'agrees'. Option 8 'motives' is a noun and ungrammatical. Option 9 'stimulates him to kill' uses the wrong sense and reads oddly. Option 10 'pushes forward' echoes 'pushes' and is ungrammatical in place.

scores.label: E
scores.note: Option 4 'nagging' is the wrong verb form and ungrammatical. Option 8 'stimulates him to kill' uses the wrong sense and reads oddly. Option 9 'incentivizes' has the wrong sense (offering a reward) and the wrong register. Option 7 is a duplicate fail.
